text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government will soon adopt measures aimed at improving the quality of Nigeria's locally made goods, head of state General Sani Abacha hinted at the weekend.

- Ernest Shonekan, chairman of Nigeria's Vision 2010 economic planning committee, has defended the size of the 172-member panel, saying the large membership will offer the project the support of all Nigerians.
- Interest rates are rising two months after the government lifted a 21 percent cap.
- Auctioning of 10,000 containers imported into Nigeria without the required paperwork will begin this month as part of moves to decongest ports before next year.
- Local council elections will be held on December 28 as the next step on the military government's plan to restore democracy, an authoratitive source said.
- Statisticians blame problem of unreliable national data on inadequate funding of the Federal Ofiice of Statistics.
- Aviation Development Company has suspended its workers without pay following the crash of a Boeing 727 which killed 143 people.

- Banks have started intense lobbying for government ministries' accounts following reports that the central bank has shortlisted 47 banks to take over when it withdraws from retail banking next year.
